analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md, adding a 'cluster waitlist' section (head lines 49-75 per the patch). The two supplied units (head lines 457-1319) are unchanged surrounding documentation and contain no modified lines. The waitlist text describes a new CLI flow (`darkbloom waitlist cluster`) in which the account joins a waitlist, nothing about the Macs is sent, and approval is manual and per account. It also says `darkbloom cluster` checks the waitlist before starting a new pair that serves through Darkbloom, and that pairs set up before the waitlist keep working. I checked this prose against the threat model. It does not alter a documented control, and the model assigns serving authorization to the platform (T-052/T-053/TB-011). I found no regression, no weakened mitigation, and no misstatement of the attestation, encryption, or prefix-cache (T-041) posture. The unchanged text in the units says public serving still requires coordinator cluster approvals and parity qualification, and local-only mode never contacts the coordinator. That matches the existing model.

Open questions for later passes (nothing in the supplied evidence shows a defect): (1) The new waitlist gate is described only as a client-side check run before first pairing. Whether the coordinator enforces account approval for cluster registration is platform-owned and not visible here. The docs must not be read as treating the client-side check as authorization. (2) The CLI waitlist implementation (`./cli-reference.md#darkbloom-waitlist`, the provider code) is not in this batch, so what the command sends and how it authenticates is unverified. The doc says it sends nothing about the Macs. (3) The threat model may want a note that the waitlist is an admission or availability gate and not a security control.
